candidates.title: Field and Laboratory Engineer (6 month fixed term)
candidates.content_text:
Who we are 
Chadwick Geotechnics is a leading supplier of testing, and engineering services to the Geotechnical, Civil and Environmental Engineering disciplines across the Eastern seaboard, New Zealand and the Asia Pacific Region.
We specialise in site investigations, geotechnical design, environmental assessments, and ground engineering solutions, as well as offering a comprehensive range of instrumentation and monitoring services. Our clients come from a diverse range of sectors, including construction, infrastructure, mining, energy, and government.
The opportunity 
We have a great role for a Field & Laboratory Engineer to support our technical team and deliver high-quality laboratory and field services across construction materials testing and geotechnical investigations. This will be an initial 6 Month Fixed Term contract engagement.
This role will suit someone who enjoys a combination of practical fieldwork, laboratory testing, technical reporting and working collaboratively within a professional engineering environment. This will involve physical and outdoor work in challenging environmental condition.
You will report to the Specialist Laboratory Engineer – Team Leader, or their delegate, and work closely with the wider Chadwick Geotechnics and Tonkin & Taylor Group teams.
What you’ll be doing 
Laboratory Testing 
Perform laboratory testing in accordance with relevant Australian and international standards and codes of practice.
Maintain knowledge of, and accreditation for, applicable NATA tests.
Develop and maintain a sound understanding of laboratory practices and operations.
Undertake training and quality assurance testing as required.
Prepare accurate test reports in accordance with company quality standards.
Enter and maintain test data in the required format, including manual and computer-based records.
Work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
Manage time and competing priorities effectively.
Fieldwork 
Assist with soil and ground investigations, including the planning and supervision of agreed field investigation programs.
Undertake soil and rock logging, sampling and in-situ testing.
Carry out field density testing where required.
Collect, verify and accurately record field data.
Complete calculations and assist with the analysis of results.
Maintain accurate field notes, site plans and chain-of-custody documentation.
Prepare figures, diagrams and plans.
Present field and laboratory data clearly and accurately.
Quality Assurance 
Assist with internal auditing and quality assurance processes to monitor compliance.
Follow company quality system requirements and contribute to maintaining a high standard of technical delivery.
Support the implementation and continuous improvement of software systems to meet the evolving needs of the business.
Perform quality assurance testing to specified standards, including laboratory testing as directed.
Health & Safety 
Comply with company HSE policies, procedures, SWMS and safe operating requirements.
Complete all required training, inductions and health assessments.
Hold a valid Construction Industry Card (CIC) and driver’s licence.
Wear and maintain company-provided PPE.
Work safely, report hazards and incidents promptly, and use equipment responsibly.
Support environmentally sustainable work practices.
What you’ll bring 
Sound literacy and numeracy skills.
An interest in construction materials testing, laboratory operations and field investigations.
The ability to follow technical procedures and relevant standards accurately.
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to quality.
Good organisational and time-management skills.
The ability to work productively both autonomously and as part of a team.
A professional approach to documentation, data management and reporting.
A commitment to workplace health and safety.
Experience in construction materials testing, geotechnical fieldwork, laboratory testing or NATA-accredited environments will be highly regarded.
Essential Requirements  
A valid driver’s licence for the vehicle you are operating.
A Construction Industry Card (CIC).
Willingness to complete all required company, project and industry training.
Why join Chad Geotechnics? 
Chadwick Geotechnics is more than just a place to work. Here, your contributions make a difference as you collaborate with experts on some of Victoria’s and Australia’s most interesting and meaningful projects, including major infrastructure, land development and renewable energy initiatives.
We embrace diversity and inclusion and offer an environment in which new ideas, innovation, technical rigour, and achievement of results are rewarded. We implement sustainability into how we operate and are committed to taking action to respond to the global and local sustainability challenges facing our natural environment and society.
Want to join the team? Apply Now!   
For further information on Chadwick Geotechnics, go to   https://www.chadwickgeotechnics.com.au . For more information on our careers go to  www.tonkintaylor.co.nz/careers . 
Chadwick Geotechnics is committed to providing equal opportunities, and a work environment which is inclusive of all. We encourage people from diverse backgrounds to apply, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

candidates.title: Site Engineer
candidates.location: South Melbourne VIC, regional project sites
candidates.content_text:
Make it yours

 Experience the excitement of building your Site Engineering career in our evolving construction company where people and performance make amazing things happen.

 Who We Are

 We're Unyte, a team of problem solvers that have seen it all and conquered the lot, delivering construction projects across the country as a principal contractor and supporting partner.

With a history stretching back decades, we focus on tailored solutions and reliable delivery in complex project environments, with one of the nation’s largest fleet of plant and operators.

Backed by the resources of Symal, a national construction group, we’re breaking new ground with limitless capability.

 The role:

 Step into a role where your engineering foundations are built on real site experience. As a Site Engineer , you’ll support the delivery of civil construction projects on the ground — working closely with Project Engineers and Supervisors to ensure works are completed safely, efficiently, and to a high standard.

This is a regionally focused role, requiring flexibility to work across project locations. If you enjoy being hands-on, solving problems in real time, and learning how projects come together on site, this is an opportunity to grow your career and make an impact.

 Your everyday:

 
Support the delivery of daily site activities, ensuring works are completed to planAssist with short-term planning, lookaheads and program updates 
Coordinate plant, materials and subcontractors to keep works running smoothlyMaintain accurate site records, including daily diaries and productivity tracking 
Support cost tracking, quantities and basic forecasting activitiesAssist with quality assurance including ITPs, inspections and documentation 
Contribute to a strong safety culture through pre-starts, risk identification and site inspectionsWork closely with Supervisors and Project Engineers to solve on-site challenges 
Build relationships with subcontractors and site teams 
Work across regional project sites as required, including periods away from home

 Who are you?

 
Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or similar1–4 years’ experience in civil construction (or relevant practical exposure) 
Strong understanding of construction fundamentals and site-based delivery 
Willingness to learn project planning, cost tracking and quality processes 
Good communication skills and ability to work within site teams 
High attention to detail and strong work ethic 
Eagerness to build a long-term career in construction 
Experience with systems like Jobpac (advantageous but not essential) 
Current driver’s licence 
Willingness and ability to work in regional locations is essential

 A career with us

 At Unyte, we've always known that people and performance make amazing things happen. Work like ours needs problem solvers, bold thinkers and genuinely good people. If you're looking for a passionate team and a pathway to career success, now's the time to make it yours.

There are plenty of good reasons to dig into a career at Unyte.

 
Forge pathways: We open doors to diverse, challenging and future-shaping construction projects to expand your experience and develop your career. 
Get ahead: From early career support and specialised learning to leadership development, we back you with tailored development programs to help you reach your goals. Success is defined by your direction and progress. 
Keep well: A healthy and happy workplace builds a brighter future. With wellness benefits, discounted health insurance, a perks and rewards platform and an industry-leading employee assistance program, we’re here to support you when you need it. 
Stay social: People are the core of Unyte. Our leading-edge work and breakout spaces stocked with snacks bring the best out of our teams and keep them fuelled for their next challenge, while our social calendar is stacked with events to connect, celebrate and reward our people.

 Diversity of thought fuels our progress

 Our inclusion offerings are designed to open doors for individuals who may not see a traditional entry point into the construction industry. We’re empowering women to thrive in construction through Shine, championing veteran career transitions through Resolve and building meaningful careers for Aboriginal people with Wamarra - helping you build a future where you belong.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, veterans and individuals from diverse cultural and life experiences are encouraged to apply.
